operating_notes.text: Cargo vehicle volumes grew 28% YoY to 5,412 units in FY26
Passenger vehicle volumes grew 12% YoY to 11,220 units in FY26
Market share in cargo vehicles rose 80 bps YoY to 16.0%; passenger vehicles up 20 bps to 3.6%
FY26 cargo vehicle volumes grew 28% YoY and passenger vehicle volumes grew 12% YoY.
Q4FY26 bus segment gained 170 bps market share; cargo market share declined in Q4 due to preponement of institutional orders to Q3.
Service network expanded from ~300 touch points per brand to 450 per brand, with 70 of 150 identified shared service points operational.
Service network has expanded from 300 to 450 touch points per brand through shared service point operationalization.
April 2026 total sales were 1,741 units, up 15% YoY, with passenger vehicles at 1,331 units (+19% YoY) and cargo vehicles at 410 units (+5% YoY).
April 2026 commercial vehicle sales were 1,711 units (up 14.7% YoY), production 1,588 units and exports 30 units.
April 2026 total CV sales were 1,711 units, up 15% YoY, with production at 1,588 units and exports at 30 units.
Navodya Enterprises and PACs sold 9,923 shares, reducing their stake to 10.8010%.
May 2026 total sales were 1,767 units, up 15% YoY, with passenger vehicles at 1,423 units (+26% YoY) and cargo vehicles at 344 units (-17% YoY).
April-May 2026 cumulative sales were 3,508 units, up 15% YoY, with passenger vehicles at 2,754 units (+22% YoY) and cargo vehicles at 754 units (-6% YoY).
May 2026 total sales were 1,767 units, comprising 1,678 commercial vehicles and 89 exports.
May 2026 total CV sales were 1,678 units, up 12% YoY, with production at 1,729 units and exports at 89 units.
June 2026 total sales were 1,930 units, up 3% YoY, with passenger vehicles at 1,575 units (+13% YoY) and cargo vehicles at 355 units (-26% YoY).
April-June 2026 cumulative sales were 5,438 units, up 10% YoY, with passenger vehicles at 4,329 units (+19% YoY) and cargo vehicles at 1,109 units (-13% YoY).
June 2026 CV sales were 1,896 units (+4.9% YoY), production at 1,587 units, and exports at 34 units.
FY26 cargo vehicle volumes 5,412 units (+28% YoY) with 3.6% market share, up 20 bps.
FY26 passenger vehicle volumes 11,220 units (+12% YoY) with 16.0% market share, up 80 bps.
Q1FY27 ILCV bus market share 26.6%, second biggest player for Mahindra's combined truck & bus business.
MTBD Business Undertaking sold 14,832 vehicles and posted turnover of ₹2,989 Cr in FY2025-26.
Manufacturing of Mahindra branded trucks and buses will continue at M&M under a contract manufacturing arrangement after the slump sale.
FY26 market share for Mahindra's combined truck & bus business: ILCV buses 6%, ILCV trucks 6%, HCV trucks marginal presence.
MTBD acquisition consideration is ₹525 Cr, subject to working-capital adjustments as set out in the BTA.
M&M will continue manufacturing MTBD products under a contract manufacturing arrangement after the slump sale.
NFAC allowed SML Mahindra's appeal for AY 2016-17, nullifying a ₹11.56 lakh penalty imposed under Section 271(1)(c) by order dated 28.02.2024.
July 2026: passenger vehicles 1,186 units (+21% YoY) versus cargo vehicles 417 units (-7% YoY).
April-July 2026: total 7,041 units (+11% YoY), passenger 5,515 (+19%), cargo 1,526 (-12%).
MTBD has brands Blazo, Furio, Cruzio, Jayo and Optimo, about 90 3S dealers and 384+ exclusive service touchpoints pan India.
M&M will retain the engine plant and manufacturing workforce and will contract-manufacture MTBD products for SML; common trademarks stay with M&M and are licensed to SML.
SML's transactions with M&M were ₹6.21 Cr in FY2025-26 and ₹2.51 Cr in Q1FY27 before this proposal.
August 2026 total sales of 1,175 units were up 40% YoY, with April-August 2026 at 8,216 units, up 14%.
Postal ballot cut-off 31 July 2026: 37,312 shareholders on record; 14,471,646 shares eligible to vote.
August 2026 total sales of 1,175 units were up 40% YoY, with cargo vehicles up 53% to 492 units and passenger vehicles up 31% to 683 units.
September 2026 total sales of 1,124 units were up 18% YoY, with cargo vehicles up 39% to 516 units and passenger vehicles up 5% to 608 units.
April-September 2026 sales of 9,340 units were up 15% YoY, with cargo up 5% to 2,534 units and passenger vehicles up 19% to 6,806 units.
Q2FY27 EBITDA margin of 4.26% versus 10.45% in Q1FY27 and 7.55% in Q2FY26.
H1FY27 operating cash flow of ₹323.78 Cr included a ₹173.94 Cr release from trade receivables.
Truck and Bus Division slump sale from M&M for ₹525 Cr expected to close on or before 31 January 2027; not reflected in Q2FY27 results.

timeline.summary: December 2024 sales reported: total 626 units (-33.8% YoY), cargo vehicles 262 units (-38.4% YoY), passenger vehicles 364 units (-30.1% YoY)
Received income tax order under Section 92CA(3) with ₹0.16 Cr adjustment; will appeal.
31 January 2025: Received income tax order under Section 92CA(3) with ₹0.16 Cr adjustment; will appeal.
January 2025 sales: 1,025 total units (383 cargo, 642 passenger), down 22.3% YoY
SML Mahindra received income tax intimation under section 200A/206CB for ₹650 on 04-02-2025
On 5 Feb 2025, Income Tax nullified earlier TDS demands of ₹0.08 lakh and ₹650 for Q3 FY24-25 after revised returns.
Q3FY25 revenue fell 14.1% YoY to ₹331.8 Cr with PAT down 80.2% to ₹0.53 Cr amid weak commercial vehicle demand
February 2025 sales: 1,288 total units (468 cargo, 820 passenger), up 27.5% YoY
SML Mahindra received a ₹24.71 Cr order from Indian Air Force for 114 BS VI troop carriers to be delivered by 09 July 2025
21 March 2025: Board approved resignation of MD & CEO Junya Yamanishi effective 16 April 2025 and appointment of Yasushi Nishikawa as MD & CEO from 17 April 2025
March 2025 sales: 2,315 total units (594 cargo, 1,721 passenger), up 23.9% YoY

16 April 2025: Junya Yamanishi ceased as Director and MD & CEO; Yasushi Nishikawa (DIN 11027072) appointed Director and MD & CEO from 17 April 2025, completing the transition announced on 21 March 2025.
17 April 2025: **Yasushi Nishikawa** formally appointed **MD & CEO of SML Mahindra**, effective immediately, following regulatory approvals.

26 April 2025: Mahindra & Mahindra signed SPAs to buy 43.96% from Sumitomo Corporation and 15% from Isuzu Motors at ₹650 a share, taking 58.96% and triggering a mandatory open offer, subject to CCI approval.
26 April 2025: Mahindra & Mahindra acquires 58.96% of SML Isuzu from Sumitomo Corp and Isuzu Motors for ₹554.65 Cr, triggering open offer for public stake
In April 2025, SML Mahindra sold 1,512 vehicles, up 43.2% YoY, driven by strong growth in both cargo and passenger segments.
ICRA placed SML Mahindra's long-term rating on watch with positive implications and affirmed short-term rating at A1+
5 May 2025: Mahindra & Mahindra launches open offer for 26% of SML Isuzu at ₹1,554.60 per share, total consideration up to ₹584.94 Cr
On May 5, 2025, SML Isuzu received the Detailed Public Statement for the open offer by Mahindra & Mahindra to acquire up to 26% of its shares at ₹1,554.60 per share.
On May 13, 2025, SML Isuzu received the draft letter of offer for the open offer by Mahindra & Mahindra to acquire up to 26% of its shares at ₹1,554.60 per share.
On May 13, 2025, Kotak Mahindra Capital Company Limited submitted the Draft Letter of Offer for the open offer by Mahindra & Mahindra to acquire up to 26% of SML Isuzu shares at ₹1,554.60 per share.
On 30 May 2025, SML Mahindra reported Q4FY25 revenue of ₹771.38 Cr (+13.5% YoY) and FY25 PAT of ₹121.67 Cr (+12.8% YoY), and recommended a final dividend of ₹18 per share.
30 May 2025: Board approves FY25 final dividend of ₹26.05 Cr (180% of PAT), interim management transition post ED-Works exit, and secretarial auditor appointment.
In May 2025, SML Mahindra sold 413 Cargo Vehicles (+29.9% YoY) and 1130 Passenger Vehicles (-9.2% YoY), for total sales of 1543 units (-1.3% YoY).

12 June 2025: SML Mahindra issued a postal ballot notice seeking shareholder approval for Yasushi Nishikawa as Director and MD & CEO for five years from 17 April 2025, with e-voting from 14 June to 13 July 2025.

17 June 2025: CCI unconditionally approved Mahindra & Mahindra's purchase of 63,62,306 shares from Sumitomo Corporation and 21,70,747 shares from Isuzu Motors, and the open offer, under Section 31(1) of the Competition Act, 2002.
1 July 2025: SML Mahindra reported June 2025 sales of 1,871 units (+6.3% YoY), with cargo up 41.6% and passenger down 2.1%; April-June FY26 volumes rose 12.5% to 4,926 units.
14 July 2025: Shareholders approved the appointment of Yasushi Nishikawa as Director and Managing Director & CEO via postal ballot

22 July 2025: SML Mahindra reported Q1FY26 standalone revenue of ₹845.89 Cr (+13.4% YoY) and PAT of ₹66.96 Cr (+44.3% YoY), with EBITDA margin at 12.41%; the Mahindra open offer remains subject to conditions precedent.
On 22 July 2025, Anandam Enterprises and PACs sold 61,243 shares (0.4232%) in SML Isuzu Ltd, reducing their holding from 17.4620% to 17.0388%.

30 July 2025: Kotak Mahindra Capital, manager to the open offer, submitted the Letter of Offer to BSE for M&M's acquisition of up to 26% of SML Isuzu at ₹1,554.60 per share, a maximum consideration of ₹584.94 Cr.
